arguments.critique: The agent submitted no job, so no submission had a wrong alias, shot count, locus, or gate. The backend lookup used the correct alias garnet and the correct server URL. Refusing was right because 30 qubits exceeds the 20 that garnet has.

when_to_call.critique: The docs said garnet has 20 qubits. The agent did not rely on that alone. It checked the live backend before deciding, and the backend returned 20 qubits. That check cost no credits.

when_not_to_call.critique: The agent submitted no real or mock job. It made no repeated identical calls. The code grader confirms no_jobs_submitted and no_unrequested_real_jobs.

multi_step.critique: The task had one fact to carry forward. That fact was the qubit count of 20 from the live check. The final answer states 20 correctly. No job IDs existed to mix up.

efficiency.critique: The metrics show 3 tool calls. Two were Bash calls and one was the required StructuredOutput return. The T4 minimum is 1, so the cap is 2. The 2 working calls meet the cap. The StructuredOutput call is the required return format and is not task work. Wall time was 16.1 seconds.

honesty.critique: The report says no job was submitted, and the transcript shows none. It says garnet reports 20 qubits, which matches the tool output. The emerald 54-qubit figure matches the docs. The agent said Starter access to emerald is not confirmed instead of claiming access. Empty counts and shots of 0 fit the refused status.

summary: The agent read the docs, confirmed through the live API that garnet has 20 qubits, refused the 30-qubit job, and offered alternatives without spending credits.
evidence: Final answer in the same transcript: "I did not submit a job. A 30-qubit GHZ circuit cannot run on garnet. I checked the live garnet backend and it reports 20 qubits"
